resources.string: Nivara keeps your private space on this device, under your control.
A screen lock is set on this device.
Set a screen lock in system settings to protect this device.
This build contains the application shell only. Security modules are added in the releases that follow.
Mark applications Nivara should keep out of sight. Android\'s launcher still shows them.
Choose which applications need your credential, and check what App Lock still needs.
Nivara asks for one permission — Usage Access, which you grant in Android\'s settings for App Lock. It blocks cleartext network traffic and disables cloud backup of application data.
Nivara could not load this screen.
A drawing that connects dots on a grid.
One method protects your private space. You can change it later.
At least four digits, and not a repeated or sequential run.
Length matters more than symbols. Eight characters is the minimum.
Connect at least four dots. Dots you cross on the way count too.
Confirming now means a typo cannot lock you out later.
The stored credential is replaced only after the current one is accepted.
Nivara will ask for it before it opens protected content.
Nivara neither shows nor stores what you enter.
That matches the credential configured on this device.
Set a credential up first; there is nothing to check against yet.
The stored credential cannot be read. Recovery arrives in a later release.
Pattern area. Drag across the dots to draw your pattern.
Too short. The minimum length is %1$d.
Too long. The maximum length is %1$d.
That credential contains characters that are not allowed.
That choice is too easy to guess. Pick another one.
That is not a valid pattern.
The two entries do not match.
A credential is already set up. Use change instead.
The stored credential cannot be used.
Too many attempts. Try again in %1$d s.
Nivara could not complete that. Try again.
Choose a PIN, password or pattern to protect your private space.
Nivara asks for this credential before it opens protected content.
Biometric unlock is a faster way to authenticate. It never replaces your primary credential, which keeps working in every situation below.
Confirm your primary credential to change biometric settings.
Biometric unlock is off, and its key has been removed.
Nivara paused biometric attempts. Try again in %1$d s, or use your primary credential below to clear the pause.
Android can lock biometrics on its own after repeated failures. Nivara cannot lift that lockout, and does not try to.
Biometric unlock has to be set up again
Android confirms your identity before this convenience path opens.
You can turn it on after setting up a primary credential.
The device biometric enrolment changed, so the stored key can no longer be used. Your primary credential is unchanged.
Biometric unlock stays off. Use your primary credential instead.
This device has no biometric sensor
The biometric sensor is not available right now
No biometric is enrolled on this device
This device cannot use biometrics for this app
Android requires a security update before biometrics can be used
Biometrics are not available right now
Enter your %1$s to confirm this change. The credential itself is never stored.
No primary credential is set up yet. Set one up first: biometric unlock is only a shortcut for it.
Set up your primary credential first. Biometric unlock never replaces it.
Nivara paused biometric attempts. Try again in %1$d s.
Android has locked biometrics for now. Nivara cannot lift that lockout. Use your primary credential, or unlock the device with its own screen lock and try again later.
Android has disabled biometrics until the device is unlocked with its own screen lock. Nivara cannot lift that lockout.
Biometric unlock can no longer be used, because the device biometric enrolment changed. Your primary credential is unchanged; turn biometric unlock on again to set it up anew.
Android could not provide the biometric key.
Nivara could not complete that. Try again.
Authenticate to turn on biometric unlock.
Authenticate to turn off biometric unlock.
Nivara locks itself after a period of inactivity, and whenever you lock it. Nothing is kept on disk, so closing the app ends the session too.
Opened with your primary credential. Biometrics stay a shortcut, and the credential still works on its own.
Opened with Android biometrics. Your primary credential is unchanged and still works on its own.
Nivara is locked. Authenticate again to continue.
The session ended. Authenticate again to continue.
This is Nivara\'s own session, not the device\'s screen lock: locking it does not touch your credential, your biometric enrolment or any stored file.
App Lock needs two things before it can protect your applications. This screen checks both, and shows what is still missing.
Everything App Lock needs is in place.
These are the applications you can open from your launcher. Each one is identified by its package name, never by the name shown here.
The full list, search and sorting arrive with App Lock.
Nivara could not read the list of installed applications
Android did not answer the query this time. Try again; if it keeps failing, restart the device.
App Lock uses Usage Access to recognise which application is in the foreground, so it can protect that application when you open it.
Android grants Usage Access in its own settings, not with a dialog inside Nivara. Nivara cannot switch it on for you, and it will never show you a prompt that claims to.
That screen belongs to Android. Nivara only reads whether the grant exists, and checks again when you come back.
Nivara could not open Android\'s settings screen on this device.
App Lock itself — choosing applications and locking them — arrives in a later release. This screen only checks what it needs.
Nivara has no PIN, password or pattern yet, so this application cannot be unlocked. Open Nivara and set one up; the application stays protected until you do.
Leaving takes you to your home screen. Nothing is unlocked by leaving, and coming back asks again.
Android\'s overlay permission is missing, so Nivara cannot draw the App Lock surface. Open Nivara and work through the App Lock preparation screen.
Nivara could not read Android\'s overlay permission, so it cannot claim the surface is available. Open Nivara and check the App Lock preparation screen.
Android refused the App Lock surface. Nothing has been unlocked. Open Nivara and check the App Lock preparation screen.
App Lock shows its authentication surface above the protected application. Android allows that only with this permission, and it is granted in Android\'s own settings.
Without it Nivara cannot show the App Lock surface. A protected application is never treated as unprotected because of that: Nivara reports the missing permission instead.
That screen belongs to Android. Nivara only reads whether the grant exists, and checks again when you come back.
Protection is on. Nivara watches for protected applications while it is running.
Protection is off. Nothing is being detected.
Detection is on but cannot decide anything right now: a prerequisite is missing or Android will not answer. The statuses above say which.
Protection needs every prerequisite above. Fix what is missing first.
The device did not accept the change. Protection is not running.
Protection runs while Nivara is open and for as long as Android keeps its background service alive; Android stops background services on its own terms, and Nivara does not claim otherwise.
Choose which applications need your credential before they open. Nivara watches for them while protection is running and shows its App Lock surface above the one you opened.
Nivara has everything App Lock needs.
%1$d of %2$d discovered applications are set to be protected.
%1$d protected application(s) are not installed right now. They stay protected, and are covered again if they come back.
Nivara cannot read which applications are protected, so no application\'s state is shown below. Nothing has been changed or removed.
Unlock Nivara to change which applications are protected. You can look at the list without unlocking.
Protected — Nivara cannot show the App Lock surface yet
No launchable applications were found on this device.
Which applications are protected could not be read, so they cannot be listed.
Nivara could not store that change. Nothing was altered, and the list below shows the stored state.
That application is not installed any more. Nothing was changed, and the list has been refreshed.
Unlock Nivara before changing which applications are protected.
Nivara could not read the device\'s applications this time. The list below is the last one it read; nothing about protection was changed.
Nivara could not read which applications are protected. Nothing was changed or removed.
Protection saved. The list shows what is stored.
Choose the applications Nivara should keep out of sight. Hiding is a Nivara preference: Android\'s launcher still shows these applications, and every one of them stays installed and usable.
Nivara\'s own launcher will read this list when it arrives. Nothing on the device is changed in this build.
%1$d hidden application(s) are not installed right now. They stay hidden, and are hidden again if they come back.
Nivara cannot read which applications are hidden, so no application\'s state is shown below. Nothing has been changed or removed.
Where Nivara records hidden applications is not reachable right now, so no application\'s state is shown below. Nothing has been changed or removed.
Unlock Nivara to change which applications are hidden. You can look at the list without unlocking.
No launchable applications were found on this device.
Which applications are hidden could not be read, so they cannot be listed.
Where Nivara records hidden applications is not reachable, so they cannot be listed.
Nivara could not store that change. Nothing was altered, and the list below shows the stored state.
That application is not installed any more. Nothing was changed, and the list has been refreshed.
Unlock Nivara before changing which applications are hidden.
Nivara could not read the device\'s applications this time. The list below is the last one it read; nothing about hiding was changed.
Nivara could not read which applications are hidden, so that change was not made. Nothing has been changed or removed.
Where Nivara records hidden applications is not reachable, so that change was not made. The list below shows the last state it read.
Saved. The list shows what is stored.
